project.name: Sample Boot Version Matrix
project.description:
Which Spring Boot versions can use Stubborn's stub runner, demonstrated rather than claimed.
Stubborn is built and tested against Boot 4.1, and sample-jetty-alignment covers that line. The question here is Boot 4.0: a consumer on 4.0 resolves Stubborn's artifacts against their own Boot, so both the Jetty classpath and Stubborn's autoconfiguration end up in an arrangement nobody tested at build time.
Every Boot 4.0 release manages Jetty on the 12.1 line, the same line as 4.1, so there is no repeat of the gh-142 minor-line split. What differs is the patch: Boot 4.0.0 is on Jetty 12.1.4 while Stubborn's BOM supplies the ee10 servlet layer at its own ${jetty.version}, currently 12.1.14. So the stub server can run an ee10 ten patches ahead of the core beneath it. gh-142 proved a minor-line gap is fatal; this sample is here to find out what a patch-level gap does, on the oldest 4.0 where the gap is widest.
boot-4-0-earliest Boot 4.0.0 — core 12.1.4, ee10 12.1.14. Widest gap. boot-4-0-latest Boot 4.0.9 — core 12.1.14, ee10 12.1.14. No gap, so a failure here would be about Boot 4.0 itself, not the gap. boot-4-1-latest Boot 4.1.2 — the line Stubborn is built against. Control.
Each module asserts the same five things: Boot's Jetty is on the 12.1 line, the ee10 Stubborn supplies shares that minor line, the application starts on Jetty and serves, the stub server starts and serves in the same JVM, and Stubborn's response-template helpers render. Each also loads the stub-runner autoconfiguration, which is the compatibility question the Jetty one hides: the starter is compiled against Boot 4.1 and has to autoconfigure against 4.0's classes.
No module configures Jetty. That is the result worth seeing: from Stubborn 0.2.1 a consumer writes no jetty-ee10-bom import and no org.eclipse.jetty exclusion, on any of these Boot versions.
Run `./mvnw clean test` here to see all three.
